messages:
jess: Heads-up: on the streaming chat canary I see slow steady growth in resident set during long tool-loop sessions. ~200MB over 4h on a single worker. Repro with the /tool-loop stress harness.
omkar: Ugh. Is that KV cache growth or general heap? Any profiler snapshots?
jess: Looks KV-adjacent. Heap profiles point to many small allocations that line up with KV slab sizes. Not classic leak (no ever-increasing unique alloc sites) — feels like reuse/pinning failure + fragmentation.
tara: Can you paste the jemalloc stats and the small-alloc histogram? Also which model/config (sequence length, batch size)?
jess: Test details: streaming chat with tool loop (10s prompt loops), model x-small-compat, dynamic batching disabled. Command I used:

```
./bench/run_streaming_canary.sh --sessions 8 --loops 250 --model x-small-compat --kv-mode streaming
```

jemalloc top:
```
allocated: 1.8G
active: 1.6G
mapped: 2.2G
metadata: 80M
small alloc buckets: spike in 512B and 1KB slabs
```

heap profile diff (summary):
- +120k allocations @512B
- +40k allocations @1KB
- steady counts for larger frames

omkar: Interesting. That suggests pages aren't being coalesced or slabs are staying pinned. Could be reference counting from active KV pages that never fully evict because of streaming prefix reuse.
chen: Also check KV pin/unpin traces. We added a codepath earlier that skips unpin for streaming contexts to avoid double-free thrash — maybe it never unpins in long dialogs.
jess: I captured a quick trace of KV ops (abbreviated):
```
KV: alloc_page slab=512 id=0x7f8a.. pinned=true owner=session-123
KV: put_chunk page=0x7f8a.. seq=1
KV: get_chunk page=0x7f8a.. seq=18
... many gets ...
(no unpin logged)
```
tara: If it's missing unpin logs, could be a control flow early-return in tool loop that skips cleanup. Any exceptions in user tools? jess: No exceptions. It's deterministic in harness.
omkar: Let's run a focused smoke test that toggles the recent 'defer_unpin_for_streams' flag. If disabling fixes growth it's likely our deferred unpin bug.
jess: I ran two back-to-back runs: with flag=true growth +200MB/4h, with flag=false growth ~20MB/4h. Logs attached to the run show explicit unpin calls when false.
chen: Ok that narrows it. But why does deferred mode hold onto so many 512B slabs? Maybe we aggregate small chunks into larger pages but mark page pinned while any chunk referenced. If chunk refs never get cleared due to sequence-number logic it will pin entire pages.
tara: Could also be eviction policy: we evict LRU pages only when > threshold, and deferred pins make them appear recently used. Consider aging-based eviction that ignores deferred pins after X minutes.
omkar: Quick patch idea: add a weak-ref style marker for deferred pins that allows eviction if there are >N deferred pins and page hasn't been touched for M seconds. Should be safe for streaming based on our latency SLOs.
jess: I prototyped an instrumentation build where deferred pins are counted separately and eviction treats them as soft. Result: long-run growth flattened to noise (~10MB drift over 6h). CPU/latency unchanged in microbench.
perf-bot: perf job #5622 completed: streaming_kv_reuse_softpin_test
perf-bot: summary: RSS delta -180MB vs baseline, p95 latency +0.3ms, CPU +1%
chen: Nice. Let's add additional safety: log a metric for softpin_count per page and a gauge for pages evicted with softpins. We'll need an e2e canary for a week.
tara: Also add a unit test that simulates tool loop early-return scenarios and asserts we unpin after T iterations.
omkar: I'll open a PR with the softpin eviction logic + metrics + unit tests. Assigning reviewers: @chen @tara
jess: Thanks all. Action items: omkar PR, run 7-day canary on canary cluster with streaming sessions, add alert if RSS growth >50MB over 8h. I'll also search other codepaths that flip the 'defer' flag.
chen: I'll review the PR tomorrow.
omkar: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/p/r/3119 (WIP) — includes perf test harness and perf-bot job link.
jess: Marking this thread resolved for now. Reopen if the canary shows regressions. :thumbsup:
